stem: Ishaan describes the same shaded rectangle of width $3$ and length $x+4$ in two ways: $3(x+4)$ and $3x+12$.

parts.text: Which claim correctly tests that the two expressions match?

options.text: Expand $3(x+4)$ to $3x+12$; both name the same whole rectangle.
The expanded form $3x+12$ is what creates the factor form $3(x+4)$.
Treat $3(x+4)$ and $3x+12$ as matching even when they describe different wholes.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Distributing gives $3\cdot x + 3\cdot 4 = 3x+12$, so both expressions measure the same rectangle.

teacher.key_rationale: Equivalence is checked by expanding to a common form for the same whole. Saying the expanded form creates the factor form reverses the test. Dropping same-whole drops the condition.
